source.title: Geometric Properties of the Voronoi Tessellation in Latent Semantic Manifolds of Large Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures a different scaling relationship: expressibility-gap estimates versus the margin threshold, not held-out cross-entropy versus model parameters, tokens, or compute. It does not test the listed loss-scaling versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports geometric-gap regressions, layer-wise correlations between cross-entropy and geometric penalties, post-hoc margin-refinement results, and downstream benchmark scores. These do not measure the claimed loss scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture sensitivity, or downstream predictability with scale or pretraining loss. The geometric-gap regression results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; benchmark and other MRP results are not rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The 'scaling law' here is the expressibility gap η(ε) versus margin threshold ε in one 4B model, not loss versus parameters, tokens or compute. No result bears on any version; the study neither tests nor uses neural scaling laws. Its passing remark that the margins are larger than those of smaller models compares across different papers and models and is not a loss-scaling measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but incomplete. The authors also conclude that Fisher MRP compresses the expressibility gap with constant collateral damage and flat benchmarks through λ=0.6. They add that its gains concentrate in head and structural tokens as λ rises. They draw nothing about loss scaling with size, data or compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study regresses an estimated geometric expressibility gap against a margin threshold and applies post-hoc geometric refinement; it does not measure held-out loss over model, data, or compute scales.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported expressibility-gap fit varies with intervention and λ_MRP; the margin-maximization run at λ_MRP=1.0 has R² = 0.9881, while the other reported fits have R² values from 0.9994 to 0.9996.

fits_no_version.finding: For Qwen3.5-4B-Base, the expressibility gap is near-linear in ε: β=0.912, R²=0.9997 (fp32). R² stays ≥0.988 after post-hoc margin refinement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mabrok's linear expressibility-gap law holds for a 4B model and persists under post-hoc margin refinement.

fits_no_version.finding: The cross-entropy/penalty correlation is negative at layers 24-28 (ρ=-0.29) and positive at layers 31-32 (ρ=0.836).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The agreement between geometric margin and cross-entropy depends on layer depth.

record.problems: The paper studies one 4B model and reports single-seed results without formal confidence intervals. Margin audits are computed on the same WikiText-103 validation corpus used for optimization, although downstream benchmarks use separate data. The authors state there is no explicit λ_MRP=0 control run. These limitations concern the paper's geometric-refinement experiments and do not make it evidence for the listed loss-scaling versions.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted from the related geometric-gap and layer-correlation findings recorded here. Other MRP churn, token-class, frequency, and benchmark results were not included because they do not measure any listed claim version or the related geometric-gap scaling finding.

untested.parts: All: no loss measured across N, D or C.
All: benchmarks are measured only across MRP strength, not across scale or pretraining loss.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper does not even discuss neural scaling laws; 'scaling law' refers to a geometric theorem. The bf16-versus-fp32 fit difference (R² 0.927 vs 0.9997) is fit sensitivity for the gap law, not for loss scaling.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run cross-entropy from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effect of depth, width, or other architecture choices on loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of the claimed loss-scaling exponents or compute-optimal split on setup and fitting choices.
